hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes Adam into divergence, so accuracy drops sharply.
At tiny learning rates training underfits within 243 epochs, so increasing the rate gives large gains.
Lowering a divergent learning rate recovers stable training and large accuracy gains.
With a small learning rate, larger batches mean fewer updates and worse underfitting.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise, which stabilizes training at high learning rates.
Smaller batches add noise on top of an already too-large step size and destabilize training.
Strong L2 penalties near 0.1 to 1 cause underfitting, so further increases hurt much more than at negligible alpha.
Deeper ReLU networks are less stable at large learning rates, so adding layers hurts more there.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so extra width helps most there and saturates at large widths.
Under strong weight decay, deeper networks compound the shrinkage of signal across layers and underfit more.
